newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends stable, could firm on HK news.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends stable, could firm on HK news.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed little changed against the U.S. dollar on Wednesday as investors moved to the sidelines after recent sluggish trade, dealers said.
Dealers said that entering 1997, the local dollar could rise in a show of optimism as Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule.

Taiwan said on Wednesday it believed Hong Kong's chief executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa could play a positive role in Taiwan-Hong Kong ties when he assumes his post after the British colony comes under Beijing's rule on July 1, 1997.
The Taiwan dollar ended at T$27.495 compared to Tuesday's T$27.497 close after moving in a narrow T$27.492-495 range.
Turnover through dealers was a frustratingly slow US$110 million. "We simply don't know what to do," said one dealer. "Almost no one has trading interest."
Stable trade was seen through the end of 1996.
"We expect rising year-end U.S. dollar demand plus U.S. dollar buying on anticipated interest rate rise on greenback," the dealer said.
"But that likely will be balanced by abundant U.S. dollar supply backed by our well-performing exports," she said.
Hong Kong's scheduled return to China may begin to trigger some U.S. dollar selling in the new year, dealers said.
"Entering 1997, especially before the Chinese new year on February 7, Taiwan's investors likely will turn optimistic, switching their foreign currency deposits to Taiwan dollars," the dealer said.
The move should push the Taiwan dollar higher so that it could test T$27.40, she said.
For Thursday, a narrow T$27.49-27.50 range was seen.
